question: What the production and technology screens write into each of their elements, how their sliders work, and where a technology goes in the tree.

addresses.name: CCountryView::Rebuild
addresses.comment: **Slot 0 of CCountryView.** Hides the view (its own slot 4), destroys the main window at +0xA8 and makes it again by the name it had, then destroys the window at +0xAC and makes it again as 'topcolor_politics' - the base's default, which CProductionView and CTechnologyView replace in their constructors. Returns 1. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: `mov edx,[eax+0x10]; call edx` on this at 0x6EB3DD; 'topcolor_politics' pushed at 0x6EB469; `mov [esi+0xac],eax; mov al,1` before the bare `ret`. What would show it wrong: a view whose second window is not a topcolor one.

addresses.name: CCountryView::Show
addresses.comment: **Slot 2 of CCountryView.** Shows the window at +0xAC, then the one at +0xA8 - each through slot 13 of the CGuiObject subobject at +0x18 - and tail-jumps to its own slot 11.
addresses.evidence: `mov ecx,[esi+0xac]; mov eax,[ecx+0x18]; mov edx,[eax+0x34]; add ecx,0x18; call edx`, the same for +0xA8, then `mov edx,[eax+0x2c]; mov ecx,esi; jmp edx` at 0x6EB380..0x6EB3AD.

addresses.name: CCountryView::UpdateCountrySkin
addresses.comment: **Slot 9 of CCountryView: the picture behind a country view changes with the country.** Builds 'gfx/interface/skins/country_bg_' + the played country's tag as text (game state +0xC30) + '.dds' and, only when FileExists says the file is there, makes a sprite from the GFX_country_bg definition with that texture and sets it on the icon `bg_countryskin` (the icon's slot 56), showing it if the window is on screen. Production and technology keep the base's body. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: '.dds' at 0x6EB5E5, 'gfx/interface/skins/country_bg_' at 0x6EB609, `call FileExists; test eax,eax; jne` at 0x6EB737, 'GFX_country_bg' at 0x6EB78E, 'bg_countryskin' at 0x6EB84A. What would show it wrong: a country with a skin file whose view shows the generic picture.

addresses.name: CCountryView::UpdateAutomationLine
addresses.comment: **Slot 11 of CCountryView.** Sets the text box `automation_setting` to what GetAutomationSettingText (0x2EB910) gives for the local player's setting for this view - `[player + 0x38][this + 0x78]` - calls its own slot 14, and enables `mode_arrow_left`, `mode_arrow_right` and `close_button` (their slot 38 with 1). Does nothing when the window has no `automation_setting`. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: 'automation_setting' at 0x6EC174, `mov esi,[edi+0x78]; call GetLocalPlayer; mov ecx,[eax+0x38]; mov esi,[ecx+esi*4]; call 0x6eb910` at 0x6EC24C, 'mode_arrow_left' 0x6EC2BA, 'mode_arrow_right' 0x6EC313, 'close_button' 0x6EC36D.

addresses.name: CCountryView::ApplyAutomation
addresses.comment: Slot 14 of CCountryView. Calls slot 38 of the main window's CGuiObject subobject with no argument when the local player's setting for this view is 1 and with 1 otherwise. **Likely** greys the view while the AI runs it; slot 38's meaning is taken from its use on buttons in slot 11. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: `cmp dword ptr [eax+esi*4],1; mov eax,[edx+0x98]; jne` at 0x6EC49B. What would settle it: reading slot 38 of CGuiObject.

addresses.no_signature: the setting arrives in ESI and the out string in a register that was not traced

addresses.name: CEconomySlider::CEconomySlider
addresses.no_signature: this is on the stack, the gui in EDX, the IC flag in CL, and a std::string is passed by value; `ret 0x28`
addresses.comment: **The slider of the production and technology screens.** Writes the observer glue vftable 0x15DE378 at +0, itself at +4 and the handler 0x7F0080 at +8; keeps the CDistributionSetting at +0x34 and `cl` at +0x3D (1 for an IC slider). Makes the window whose name it is handed, sets `title` to the setting's slot 6, attaches itself to the scrollbar `actual_slider`, renames the window to its index in decimal, attaches itself to `ic_need_button` if the window has one and calls slot 65 on `limit` if it has one. No RTTI of its own: the name is the glue's, VCEconomySlider::__CButtonObserverGlue.
addresses.evidence: `mov dword ptr [edi],0x15de378; mov [edi+4],edi; mov dword ptr [edi+8],0x7f0080` at 0x7EFC68; 'title' 0x7EFCE2, 'actual_slider' 0x7EFD7E, `push 0xa ... call _itoa` at 0x7EFDE5, 'ic_need_button' 0x7EFE44, 'limit' 0x7EFEDD. Its two callers allocate 0x40 bytes first (0x7FC4DE, 0x81A5B0).

addresses.name: CEconomySlider::ResetFromSetting
addresses.comment: Puts the slider where its setting says: reads the setting's share at +8 (a 48.15 fixed point, through `fild qword` and 2^-15), multiplies by the slider's maximum, sets that value and updates the texts. If the scrollbar's +0x253 is set it enables the slider's own button again and clears the byte. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: `mov eax,[esi+0x34]; mov ecx,[eax+8]; mov edx,[eax+0xc]; fild qword; fmul qword ptr [0x160a2e0]` (3.0517578125e-05) at 0x7EFFAD, then 0x7F0D90, 0x7F0CC0 and 0x7F0290.

addresses.name: CEconomySlider::OnNeedButton
addresses.comment: **What `ic_need_button` does.** If the setting's slot 7 says it has a window of its own - only lend-lease's does - calls its slot 8 and returns. Otherwise sets the slider to need + half a step, the need being the setting's slot 3 and the step the scrollbar's +0x234 over a thousand; then disables the slider's own button and sets +0x3E, pinning it to its need - unless the button was already disabled (its slot 44 answering 3), in which case it is enabled again if the scrollbar's +0x253 is set. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: `mov edx,[eax+0x1c]; call edx; test al,al; je` then `mov edx,[eax+0x20]` at 0x7F0090; `mov eax,[eax+0xc]` for slot 3 and `fild qword ptr [eax]; fmul qword ptr [0x160a2e0]`; `cmp eax,3; sete` after slot 44; `mov edx,[eax+0xbc]; call edx; mov byte ptr [esi+0x3e],1` at the end.

addresses.name: CEconomySlider::Update
addresses.comment: **Fills a slider's three elements.** The scrollbar's value v, an amount of IC or of leadership, is made a share - v * 32768 rounded, over TotalIC (+0x604) when +0x3D is set and over TotalLeadership / 1000 (+0xBD8) when not. `value` = the setting's slot 2 for that share, a colour escape, followed by v to two decimals. `need` = the setting's slot 1 for that share. `limit`, when the window has one and the setting's slot 11 is nought or more, is shown and moved along the slider to that value; hidden otherwise. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: 'actual_slider' 0x7F02C3; `cmp byte ptr [edi+0x3d],bl` at 0x7F0374 choosing +0x604 or +0xBD8; 'value' 0x7F05DA with `mov eax,[eax+8]` on the setting at 0x7F0670 and operator+ at 0x7F0694; 'need' 0x7F074C with `mov eax,[eax+4]` at 0x7F07E2; 'limit' 0x7F0880 with `mov eax,[edx+0x2c]` at 0x7F08C2 and `fldz; fcompi`. What would show it wrong: a slider whose figure is a percentage.

addresses.name: CEconomySlider::GetValue
addresses.no_signature: the slider is on the stack and the float comes back in XMM0
addresses.comment: The slider's value as a float: slot 4 of the scrollbar `actual_slider`'s subobject at +0x48. `ret 4`. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: 'actual_slider', `lea ecx,[eax+0x48]; mov eax,[ecx]; mov edx,[eax+0x10]; call edx; fstp dword ptr [ebp+8]; movss xmm0,[ebp+8]`.

addresses.name: CEconomySlider::SetValue
addresses.comment: Sets the slider: hands the scrollbar's subobject at +0x48 `floor((value + 0.0005) * 1000)` through its slot 7 and keeps the float at +0x38. `ret 8`. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: `addsd xmm0,[0x160a460]` (0.0005), `mulsd xmm0,[0x160a300]` (1000), floorf, _ftol2_sse, `mov eax,[edx+0x1c]; lea ecx,[esi+0x48]; call eax`, `movss [ebx+0x38],xmm0`.

addresses.name: CEconomySlider::GetMaximum
addresses.no_signature: the slider is on the stack and the float comes back in XMM0
addresses.comment: The slider's maximum: the scrollbar's +0x230 over a thousand, rounded to the hundredth with the sign put back. `ret 4`. The name is ours, and that +0x230 is the maximum is read off this and SetMaximum rather than off the scrollbar.
addresses.evidence: `movd xmm0,[eax+0x230]; cvtdq2ps; divsd [0x160a300]`, `mulsd [0x160a358]` (100), `addsd [0x160a308]` (0.5), cvttsd2si, `divsd [0x160a358]`. Likely, and why: both views take the total left to hand out as this minus the sum of the values.

addresses.name: CEconomySlider::SetMaximum
addresses.comment: Gives the scrollbar a new range: reads its +0x234 and +0x22C, makes the argument thousandths the way SetValue does, and calls slot 5 of the subobject at +0x48 with the three. Both views call it with the country's total - TotalIC, or TotalLeadership over a thousand - so the 0 to 100 of the .gui file is replaced. `ret 4`. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: Three lookups of 'actual_slider', reading +0x234, +0x22C and then `movss xmm0,[ebp+8]`; `mov edx,[edi+0x14]; call edx`. Callers: 0x7FE050 and 0x7FF98D with `[edi+0xc8]`, 0x81B740 with `[edi+0xcc]`. Likely, and why: which of the three is which was not read off the scrollbar.

addresses.name: CEconomySlider::IsDisabled
addresses.comment: Whether the slider's own button (the scrollbar's +0xA0) answers 3 to slot 44 - disabled, which is what the need button does to it. A disabled slider is left out when the views share out what is left. `ret 4`. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: `mov ecx,[eax+0xa0]; mov eax,[ecx]; mov edx,[eax+0xb0]; call edx; cmp eax,3; sete`. Likely, and why: that state 3 is disabled is from OnNeedButton calling slot 47 (+0xBC) to produce it and slot 46 (+0xB8) to undo it.

addresses.name: CEconomySlider::IsHeld
addresses.comment: True when +0x3C is set, or when the slider's own button answers 1, 4 or 5 to slot 44. **Likely** "the player has hold of it": the views do not push a slider this is true of. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: `cmp byte ptr [esi+0x3c],0; je; mov al,1`, then three lookups each followed by slot 44 and `cmp eax,ebx` with ebx 1, `cmp eax,4`, `cmp eax,5`. What would settle it: the button's state numbers.

addresses.name: CEconomySlider::LatchMoved
addresses.comment: Moves the scrollbar's byte at +0x252 into the slider's +0x3C and clears it at the scrollbar. Called by both views straight after Update on every slider. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: `mov cl,[eax+0x252]; mov byte ptr [eax+0x252],bl; mov [esi+0x3c],cl` at 0x7F135B..0x7F136E.

addresses.name: CDistributeProduction::GetValueColour
addresses.comment: **Slot 2: the colour of the slider's `value` line.** A std::string of two characters: the escape for red (a7 52, 0x15B5C58) when the need is greater than what the share gives, both cut to the hundredth, and for white (a7 57, 0x15B6700) otherwise. `ret 0xC`: the out string and the share, a 48.15 fixed point in two dwords. CEconomySlider::Update puts the figure after it. Here the share is turned into IC - TotalIC (+0x604) times the share - and compared with the need at +0x20. **Renamed 2026-10-08 from GetICForShare**, which was read only as far as that multiply and recorded as returning a CFixedPoint; it returns the string. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countryviews.md.
addresses.evidence: `cmp eax,edi; jle 0x51a576; push 0x15b5c58; call std::string::assign; mov eax,esi; ret 0xc` and the other arm with 0x15B6700. The two values compared are each `* 1000 / 10000` of a thousandths figure. What would show it wrong: a caller reading eight bytes of number out of the result.
addresses.revises: GetICForShare was read only as far as its first multiply and given a CFixedPoint result; the body ends by assigning a two-character colour escape to the out string

CEconomySlider::Update puts the figure after it. Here the need is the class's own slot 3. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: `mov edx,[edx+0xc]; call edx` on this for the need, then `cmp eax,esi; jle` choosing 0x15B5C58 or 0x15B6700; `ret 0xc`.

addresses.name: CDistributeReinforcement::GetNeeded
addresses.comment: **Slot 3: the slider's need**, a 48.15 fixed point written as two dwords through the out pointer; `ret 4`. Reinforcement's is the country's reinforcement_cost (+0xA98), thousandths shifted thirty and divided by 0x1F40000. **Renamed 2026-10-08 from GetNeedTooltip**: this was recorded as a slot 3 body that builds from SLIDER_NEED and returns with `ret 0xC`, which is the function two bytes of padding after it, 0x11CB00, at slot 1. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countryviews.md, section 3.
addresses.evidence: The whole body is 0x2E bytes: `mov eax,[ecx+0x18]; mov eax,[eax+0xa98]; cdq; shld edx,eax,0x1e; push 0; push 0x1f40000; shl eax,0x1e; push edx; push eax; call __alldiv; mov ecx,[ebp+8]; mov [ecx],eax; mov [ecx+4],edx; mov eax,ecx; pop ebp; ret 4`. No string is touched.
addresses.revises: recorded as the SLIDER_NEED body with ret 0xC; that is 0x11CB00, the next function. This one is 0x2E bytes, writes a 64-bit number and ends ret 4

addresses.name: CDistributeResearch::ShareAmongProjects
addresses.comment: **Slot 4 of CDistributeResearch: which projects on the queue get leadership.** The research leadership - TotalLeadership times the share at +8 times the factor at +0x10 - is walked down CurrentResearch (+0x638): each technology that passes CTechnology::CheckResearchAllowed takes a whole point (0x8000) or what is left if less, written in thousandths to the technology status's leadership_by_technology (+0x238); one that fails, or comes after the leadership has run out, gets nought. The research queue's three backgrounds read that back. The other nine classes leave slot 4 as the shared no-op. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: `mov eax,0x8000` and the 64-bit compare at 0x51F5A0, `sub [esp+0x18],eax; sbb esi,ecx`, then `mov [edx+ecx*4],eax` into +0x238 by the technology's +0x244; the other arm stores 0. Likely, and why: read from a filtered listing, and the caller was not found.

addresses.name: CProductionView::SetGoodsText
